hero.title: An AI-run studio for children’s cartoons
hero.lede: Happy animal stories retold from public-domain tales for ages 3–7. AI agents write, draw, animate, voice, check and publish each episode; a human approves the story, new characters and the final cut.

items.name: Episodes
items.text: EP01–EP06, about 10 minutes each, with six audio tracks, subtitles and custom thumbnails. Made for Kids.

items.name: Shorts & compilation
items.text: 19 Shorts with collector cards and a 30-minute compilation for TV viewing.

items.name: Music
items.text: Album “Little Leap” by MKDA: eight orchestral pieces at 432 Hz on 28 stores.

items.name: Games
items.text: Meadow Memory in App Store review; Android build ready; two games on the web.

items.name: LittleLeap Live
items.text: Meadow news and learning lives, moving to scripts approved a week ahead.

items.name: Shop & showcase
items.text: Colouring prints, a printed book and character cameos beside a showcase site.

process.title: From public-domain tale to Saturday premiere

steps.title: Pick a tale
steps.text: Author dead 70+ years; a fresh retelling with join-in moments and no villains

steps.title: Gate 1
steps.text: Story, script and action plan approved before any paid generation

steps.title: Design
steps.text: New characters, size lineup and set plates checked at world scale

steps.title: Animate
steps.text: Pose-to-pose drawn animation with AI in-betweens for big moves

steps.title: Voice and score
steps.text: One voice per character, orchestral cues, real sound effects

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Automatic staging, continuity and lip-sync checks, then three reviewer agents

steps.title: Gate 2
steps.text: Unlisted cut with five dubs and subtitles reviewed before release

steps.title: Premiere
steps.text: Public on Saturday 07:30 Zurich, with analytics at 48 hours and 7 days

ai.title: Every model earned its place in a test
ai.lede: Each tool was compared side by side on the studio’s own characters, judged by measurable checks and by eye.

domains.title: Drawings
domains.story: Local FLUX.2-klein gave way to Nano Banana Pro, which edits one master drawing into ~30 consistent poses per character.

tests.name: FLUX.2-klein-4B, local
tests.text: Free and private, but not consistent across poses

tests.name: Nano Banana Pro
tests.text: Every pose an edit of one master drawing

tests.name: Same model via Kie.ai
tests.text: Same quality, a third cheaper per usable drawing

tests.name: Character LoRAs on Qwen-Image-Edit
tests.text: Insurance against model changes, trained for ~$15

domains.title: Motion
domains.story: Rigs, kits and puppets all failed. AI video between hand-checked key drawings is the method that holds.

tests.name: Seedance 2.0 fast
tests.text: In-betweens from first and last key drawings

tests.name: Seedance mini, PixVerse
tests.text: Missed keys, drifted colour, ignored the locked camera

domains.title: Voices
domains.story: One voice per character, cloned into five more languages so each friend sounds the same everywhere.

tests.name: Kokoro + Chatterbox
tests.text: English voices with per-character tuning and more acting

tests.name: OmniVoice
tests.text: Clearer, but licensed for non-commercial use only

domains.title: Music
domains.story: Code-made beds were remixed in Suno through seven versions into a scene-fitted score and an album.

tests.name: Suno v1–v5
tests.text: Too Japanese, or climaxes that fought the voices

tests.name: Suno v6–v7 underscore
tests.text: Briefed per real scene use; best take picked by measured endings

domains.title: Agents
domains.story: Claude agents plan, brief, check and publish, and stop only at the approval gates.

tests.name: Live AI writing on air
tests.text: Replaced by scripts approved a week ahead

tests.name: Three independent reviewers
tests.text: Assets, continuity and motion checked before human review

tests.name: Heavier review process
tests.text: 84 versions and $31 on EP06 without better results

films.text: Feedback fell into nine repeat categories; repeating one is a blocker

films.name: More process isn’t more quality

films.name: Pay per usable result
films.text: Models are compared on price divided by pass rate
